tagline: Up the Snoqualmie on the old Yellowstone Trail.
intro: Out of Woodinville, SR 202 goes south through the Sammamish River valley through a district of wineries and tasting rooms, past Marymoor Park by the north shore of Lake Sammamish and around the Sammamish Plateau by Patterson Creek. At Fall City it crosses the Snoqualmie River and follows it upstream, takes a long hairpin over Tokul Creek, passes the falls and comes through Snoqualmie and the Three Forks lowlands into North Bend.

It is an old way through. Wagon roads ran beside the 1889 railroad by 1902, and in the 1910s the stretch from Redmond to North Bend became part of the Yellowstone Trail, with a piece near Redmond paved in brick in 1913.
season: State of Washington Tourism suggests fall, for the golden and red foliage.

moments.title: Snoqualmie Falls
moments.text: Most of the river goes to the power plants, but high water pours across the whole 268-foot face, which the Snoqualmie hold to be where First Woman and First Man were created.

moments.title: Northwest Railway Museum, Snoqualmie
moments.text: The 1890 depot was dressed up with scrollwork to suit Seattle vacationers coming out to see the falls, and the museum's railway runs on 5.5 miles of the original line.

moments.title: North Bend
moments.text: Mount Si, named for the homesteader Josiah "Uncle Si" Merritt, towers over the town and turned up in the opening credits of Twin Peaks, which was filmed here.
